done.item: 2. FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY: AES-256-GCM under a key made for each file, a header with format version and key id, earlier plain files stay readable, scripts/encrypt-files.mjs
done.how: src/server/filecrypt.ts holds the format and is shared by the server and the script. An encrypted file is "\0enc", version 1, an 8-byte key id (an HMAC of the key, which says nothing about the key), a 16-byte salt, a 12-byte nonce, a 4-byte header check, then the contents and the GCM tag. The key for each file is HKDF-SHA256 of the server's key with the salt and the file's name. The header and the name are part of what GCM checks. Every write goes to a temporary file, is flushed to the disk, then renamed into place in one step. Plain files written before stay readable. scripts/encrypt-files.mjs, for each file: encrypts it into a hidden temporary file, flushes it, reads it back and checks it with the current key and the fingerprint, checks that the original has not changed since it was read, then renames over it. It has --check and --new-key, reads .env.local and .env as the server does, allows one run at a time (a lock left by a run that was killed is taken over), clears half-written copies left by an earlier run, and names damaged files and files under keys it does not have, leaving them as they are. Exit codes: 0 when done, 1 when something needs a look, 2 when a setting is wrong. How to make a key (openssl rand -base64 32) is in .env.example, the README and the script.

done.item: 4. Nothing lost by a mistake with the key: loud at start, no new files written until the old key is listed, damaged files reported and never served, no key works as today
done.how: At start, instrumentation.ts calls fileStoreWarning(), which reads the first 45 bytes of every stored file. If any file was written with a key the server does not hold, or FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set to something that is not a key, it logs 'STORING FILES IS STOPPED' with the key ids (never the keys), files an alert in the operator queue and emails SUPPORT_EMAIL and OPERATOR_EMAILS. From then on every write answers 503 "storage_stopped" with plain words that nothing was saved and nothing is lost; reads go on wherever they can. A correction that asks someone to sign again also waits with 503, because otherwise the copy of what they signed would be lost (one line in correctEnvelope). Signing still finishes, and the timer makes the signed PDF once files can be stored again. A file under a key nobody listed that turns up after the start stops writes from then on. An uploaded file that only looks encrypted cannot cause a stop: a file whose bytes match its own name is always plain. Every read checks the file, plain or encrypted. A damaged file answers 500 "file_damaged", a file whose key is missing answers 503 "file_locked", and each damaged or missing file is reported once (log, queue, email). The export leaves an unreadable signed PDF out and names it in README.txt. Storing a file that is already there with the same contents replaces a damaged copy. The warning also says what to do if a key is lost for good. With no key and no encrypted file in the folder, behaviour is as before, apart from the new check on reads and atomic writes.

build:encrypt.notes_for_integrator:
Changes others will notice:
- Every read of a stored file is now checked against its SHA-256 name, with or without a key. A missing or changed file used to throw ENOENT or be served as it was. Now it answers HttpError 500 {code:'file_damaged'} in plain words, and a one-time alert goes to the operator queue (support_requests row named 'Sign&Grow (automatic alert)'), to the log, and by email to SUPPORT_EMAIL/OPERATOR_EMAILS.
- Writes are atomic (temporary file, fsync, rename). Storing contents that are already there now reads the existing copy and replaces it if it is damaged.
- While storing is stopped, a correction that asks someone to sign again answers 503 storage_stopped and saves nothing.
- At start the server reads the first 45 bytes of every stored file. I have not timed this on a very large folder.

Decisions the owner should confirm:
- A server with no key, finding encrypted files it cannot read, also stops storing files. That is stricter than "no key means as today", but otherwise new plain files would be mixed with files nobody can open, while the operator may believe everything is encrypted.
- I added no row to "What the bad reviews taught us". research/complaints.json has no complaint about encryption at rest, and I would not invent one.

For the rename pass:
- The constants in src/server/filecrypt.ts ('stored file key id', 'stored file v1 ...', the magic bytes) contain no product name on purpose: changing any of them would make every encrypted file unreadable. The test file checks this.
- The alert name 'Sign&Grow (automatic alert)' now appears in filestore.ts as well as routes-support.ts and routes-billing.ts. All three must be renamed together.
- The new copy says Sign&Grow where it names the product.

Left open:
(1) On the signing page, the document viewer in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx shows its generic "The document could not be opened here... download it" for a locked or damaged file. The Download button then gets the 503/500 JSON. Showing the server's message there would need an edit in that busy file.
(2) The server never removes its own half-written temporary files (.<sha>.w<pid>-<hex>) left by a crash; only the script clears them, once they are an hour old.
(3) Running the script while the server runs leaves a tiny window in which a file the server deletes could come back encrypted. A check before the swap narrows it, and the README and the script say to stop the server first.
(4) There is no decrypt script, and the database is never encrypted (by design; documented).
(5) Someone with write access to the disk could stop storing by dropping a fake file, but with disk access they already have everything.
(6) The email to operators is sent through a dynamic import('./mail.ts'). The tests confirm it under node, but in next dev only the branch without an operator address was seen.
